proposals.before: When histories of several generations are thus, their deeds grow dim: even rulers who rode with the times to win fame and ministers who plotted together have none who could plainly stir the eyes and ears of the world and claim the mouths of the world.
proposals.after: When histories of several generations are thus, their deeds grow dim: even among rulers who rode with the times to win fame and ministers who plotted together, none could plainly stir the eyes and ears of the world and claim the mouths of the world.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical: 'have none who could' makes the rulers/ministers the possessors of an absent subject; the Chinese means none of those figures achieved such renown.

decisions.reason: Chinese 雖有…之君…之臣，未有…者也 means that although such rulers and ministers existed, none of them achieved renown that stirred the world's eyes and ears; the original 'have none who could' misconstrues that construction, and the proposed 'even among…, none could…' restores the sense accurately.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雖有隨世以就功名之君，相與合謀之臣，未有赫然得傾動天下之耳目，播天下之口者也
